雰.meaning: A theatre makes soft, misty <part>rain</part> fall indoors over the stage, but only for one <part>part</part> of the play: the farewell scene. The lights dim and the audience sniffles. Nobody remembers the words afterwards, only the <kanji>atmosphere</kanji>.
雰.on: On opening night the rain machine jams and blows a full ty<sound>phoon</sound> into the front row.

剖.meaning: Twins argue over the last pie, so their granny climbs onto a <part>soapbox</part> in the kitchen, raises a butter knife like a <part>dagger</part> and gives a speech about fairness. Then, with one neat cut, she makes two exact halves. That's how you <kanji>divide</kanji>.
剖.on: The pie is as heavy as a <sound>bo</sound>ulder: each half still needs two hands.

猶.meaning: A magician pulls a <part>fishhook</part> from his hat. Then a rubber duck. Then a stick of <part>lit dynamite</part> that fizzes out into confetti. 'And <kanji>furthermore</kanji>…' he says, reaching in again, as the audience edges toward the door.
猶.on: The next thing out of the hat is a small, grumpy <sound>u</sound>nicorn.
猶.kun: It munches the front row's <sound>na</sound>chos, and the crowd gasps: '<sound>Oh</sound>!'

稽.meaning: A baker with a <part>broken crutch</part> hobbles to the mill every morning for <part>grain</part> and bakes the same loaf again and again. Burnt, flat, burnt, flat, until loaf three hundred comes out <part>delicious</part>. Nothing beats <kanji>practice</kanji>.
稽.on: To celebrate, loaf three hundred and one is a birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke.
稽.kun: He tucks a pink <sound>carn</sound>ation behind his ear and sniffs a bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic, dreaming up the next recipe.

遭.meaning: An <part>office</part> worker on a wheelie chair rolls down the wheelchair <part>ramp</part> outside just as his boss rolls up it on hers. Crash: chairs locked, noses touching. What a way to <kanji>meet</kanji>.
遭.on: Someone had left a bar of <sound>so</sound>ap at the bottom of the ramp.
遭.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>… <sound>oo</sound>ps,' says the boss, still nose to nose with him.

亭.meaning: A tea seller in the park builds a hut from junk: a saucepan <part>lid</part> on the tip, a little <part>mouth</part> of a hatch to pass cups through, a <part>blanket</part> stretched as the roof, all propped on an old <part>street</part> sign. People queue at the wobbliest <kanji>pavilion</kanji> in town.
亭.on: When it rains, he holds it together with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.

轄.meaning: A toy <part>car</part> zooms round the kitchen, bumping ankles and doing <part>harm</part> to the cat's tail. Grandpa grabs the remote, taps one button, and it parks politely by the fridge. He is the one in <kanji>control</kanji>.
轄.on: As a reward, he lets it carry a slice of chicken <sound>katsu</sound> to the cat.
轄.kun: Just in case, the <sound>coo</sound>k jams a <sound>sa</sound>lsa lid under its wheel, and a <sound>bee</sound> sits on top to guard it.

藻.meaning: A crab wants a <part>treehouse</part>, but trees don't grow on the seabed. So among the <part>water drops</part> it plants floppy green <part>grass</part> that sways with the tide, and builds its house up top. It lives in a forest of <kanji>seaweed</kanji>.
藻.on: Every evening it scrubs the slime off with a bar of <sound>so</sound>ap.
藻.kun: A lobster borrows a long strand to <sound>mo</sound>p the crab's floor.

宛.meaning: Under the post office <part>roof</part>, a <part>sleeping cat</part> naps on top of the parcel pile. The postman, half asleep himself, delivers the cat along with the parcels. At the door it yawns, reads the label and moves in: it was the right <kanji>address</kanji> after all.
宛.on: Curled on its new sofa, it purrs louder than a truck <sound>en</sound>gine.
宛.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' sighs the new owner, and sends the post office a <sound>te</sound>xt: more cats, please.

匹.meaning: In a sock <part>drawer</part>, a lonely sock on little <part>legs</part> searches every corner for its twin. At last it finds one exactly the same: same stripes, same hole in the toe. A perfect <kanji>equal</kanji>.
匹.on: The pair hop out and thumb a ride by the road like a <sound>hitch</sound>hiker.
匹.kun: The driver, in high <sound>hee</sound>ls, counts her passengers: two dogs, a <sound>ki</sound>wi bird and two socks. A count of small animals.

侶.meaning: In a science classroom, a plastic skeleton's <part>spine</part> hangs from a <part>coat hook</part> by the door. A lonely janitor chats to it every night, offers it tea and tells it jokes. After thirty years, it's his best <kanji>companion</kanji>.
侶.on: On his last night before retiring, he pours it a glass of <sound>Rio</sound>ja.
侶.kun: He sets a <sound>to</sound>p hat on its skull and leans his <sound>mo</sound>p beside it.

繕.meaning: Every night a <part>virtuous</part> scarecrow climbs off its pole and, with a needle and <part>thread</part>, quietly fixes the holes in the farmer's socks. By morning they are whole again. Nobody knows who does the <kanji>darning</kanji>.
繕.on: Then it rakes the farmer's <sound>zen</sound> garden into neat lines.
繕.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' it sneezes in the straw dust, then mends the <sound>coo</sound>k's apron and a <sound>ro</sound>bin's torn nest.

朽.meaning: A walking <part>cane</part> carved from an old <part>tree</part> leans in a damp corner for fifty years. Mushrooms sprout on the handle, beetles tunnel through, and one day it folds in two like soft bread. Wood never wins against <kanji>decay</kanji>.
朽.on: The billiard <sound>cue</sound> beside it is just as soft.
朽.kun: The <sound>coo</sound>k uses the crumbly wood to smoke his <sound>chee</sound>se.

碁.meaning: Grandpa's <part>bookshelf</part> holds no books, only bowls of black and white <part>stone</part> counters. Every evening he lays out a wooden grid, and he and the cat take turns placing them, each trying to surround the other. It's their game of <kanji>Go</kanji>.
碁.on: The cat plays in swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles so grandpa can't read its eyes.

寛.meaning: A goat climbs onto the <part>roof</part>, eats the <part>grass</part> sprouting in the gutters, then chews the strap of the family's security <part>camera</part>. The owner just waves at the screen and laughs. She's very <kanji>tolerant</kanji>.
寛.on: She even leaves it a pink <sound>car</sound>nation for dessert.
寛.kun: Full, the goat stretches out like a <sound>coo</sound>k after lunch, sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' and dozes beside a <sound>ro</sound>bin.

窒.meaning: A gopher keeps popping out of a <part>hole</part> in the stage during the mayor's speech. Fed up, she drags her <part>podium</part> over and stands it right on top. The gopher grumbles and digs a new exit: she has managed to <kanji>plug up</kanji> the hole.
窒.on: It pops up in the flowerbed chewing <sound>chee</sound>se and sneezes: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

艇.meaning: The whole <part>imperial court</part>, crowns, robes and all, crams into one tiny <part>boat</part> to cross the palace moat because the bridge is closed. The emperor himself has to take an oar. It's the most royal <kanji>rowboat</kanji> ever.
艇.on: It leaks, so the empress patches it with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.

班.meaning: Two chess pieces, each a <part>king</part>, stand on either side of a <part>dagger</part> stuck in the board and split the pawns into teams: left side yours, right side mine. Each team marches off as its own <kanji>squad</kanji>.
班.on: The squad that wins the game gets a pot of <sound>hon</sound>ey.

賠.meaning: A clam, the <part>shellfish</part> a tourist trod on, climbs onto a <part>soapbox</part> on the beach and shouts: 'Pay up!' The tourist hands over a shiny new shell and half a sandwich. The clam calls it fair <kanji>compensation</kanji>.
賠.on: Then it rides off on the tourist's <sound>bi</sound>ke.

肖.meaning: A cook flips a fried egg so high that it hangs in the night sky beside the <part>moon</part>, with a <part>sparkle</part> of hot oil around it. An owl looks from one to the other, totally confused. It's an uncanny <kanji>resemblance</kanji>.
肖.on: The neighbours come out to watch the <sound>show</sound>.
肖.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, <sound>ya</sound>, me too!' says one, and <sound>ca</sound>lmly flips her own egg, hoping the same luck rubs off: to share in good fortune.

赴.meaning: A marathon <part>runner</part> spots a dripping <part>faucet</part> at mile ten. She stops, turns it off tight, nods once, and carries on toward the finish line, steady as a clock. Nothing stops her for long: on she will <kanji>proceed</kanji>.
赴.on: At the finish line she flops onto a <sound>fu</sound>ton.
赴.kun: An <sound>o</sound>tter, a <sound>mo</sound>p-haired dog and a <sound>moo</sound>se jog along behind her.

痕.meaning: A <part>robot</part> stores itself in a <part>leaky shed</part> every winter: drip, drip, drip on its head all season. In spring it rolls out with one perfect rusty ring on its forehead, a <kanji>mark</kanji> it can never polish off.
痕.on: A <sound>con</sound>dor lands on its head and pecks at the ring, thinking it's a coin.
痕.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' sighs the robot, and wipes the <sound>to</sound>p of its head.

丹.meaning: Deep in a cave, a miner takes one <part>slash</part> at the wall with her <part>crowbar</part>, and a single <part>dot</part> of red ore pops out. She draws <part>one</part> line across the rock with it. The stripe glows the colour of old iron: <kanji>rust-colored</kanji>.
丹.on: She follows the stripe deeper into the <sound>tun</sound>nel.
丹.kun: Kneeling at the wall, she finds red dust coating both <sound>knee</sound>s.

斎.meaning: Before anyone may climb the temple's tall <part>ladder</part> down to the <part>altar</part>, they must wash on every rung: hands on rung one, feet on two, ears on three. By the bottom they squeak. That ladder is a climb of <kanji>purification</kanji>.
斎.on: At the altar, a monk hands out cups of apple <sound>ci</sound>der.
斎.kun: On <sound>to</sound>p of the altar waits a plain meal of rice and one <sound>ki</sound>wi: a temple meal.

俸.meaning: On payday, a lighthouse keeper finds a bag of coins hanging on his <part>coat hook</part>: the town's monthly <part>offer</part> for keeping the light on. It's not much, but it comes every month: his <kanji>stipend</kanji>.
俸.on: He spends it on a new garden <sound>ho</sound>se to wash the lamp.

款.meaning: A grumpy <part>gentleman</part> leaves a plum pie on the little garden <part>altar</part> next door, where his rival meditates. The rival wakes with a giant <part>yawn</part>, smells pie, and waves over the fence. Their old feud melts into <kanji>goodwill</kanji>.
款.on: Next morning a pink <sound>car</sound>nation sits on the gentleman's doorstep.

痩.meaning: A snowman hides in a <part>leaky shed</part> to escape the sun, but warm drips and the heat of the <part>lantern holder</part> hanging above slowly melt him. By spring he's a carrot on a stick. He did want to <kanji>get thin</kanji>, just not that thin.
痩.on: The kids wash his scarf with a bar of <sound>so</sound>ap and save it for next winter.
痩.kun: '<sound>Ya</sound>,' he gurgles, '<sound>se</sound>nd me to the freezer.'

紺.meaning: A tailor balances two buckets on a <part>yoke</part>, one of ink and one of sea water, and dips her <part>thread</part> in both. It comes out the colour of the sky an hour after sunset. Every sailor's coat in town is stitched in that <kanji>dark blue</kanji>.
紺.on: A <sound>con</sound>dor in a navy coat perches on the tailor's yoke, admiring its own sleeves.

宵.meaning: Long after midnight, the cook climbs onto her <part>roof</part> with a frying pan. The egg she flips up there bears such a <part>resemblance</part> to the moon that the stars blink. Only owls and cooks are awake in the <kanji>wee hours</kanji>.
宵.on: The owls hoot a standing ovation: best <sound>show</sound> of the night.
宵.kun: Back at dusk, an owl was doing <sound>yo</sound>-yo tricks for an <sound>ea</sound>gle.

惰.meaning: A sloth in a hammock has a <part>heartbeat</part> so slow that the vet's monitor barely blips. It has lain on its <part>left</part> side since the last full <part>moon</part>, because turning over sounds like work. Champion of the <kanji>lazy</kanji>.
惰.on: A <sound>du</sound>ck kindly paddles over and nudges it onto its back.
